validity.recommendation: Keep the entity; it is a real, correctly-classified gas transmission trunk (not a duplicate).
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solidly confirmed. This is the well-documented Iran-Pakistan ('Peace'/IP) gas pipeline. Iran's ~900-1,172 km 56-inch section from the Pars energy zone to Iranshahr near the Pakistan border is physically built/largely complete; the Pakistan side (border->Nawabshah) is not. Multiple independent sources describe it in detail (offshore-technology.com, en.wikipedia, dialogue.earth). Not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct - a cross-border gas (Fuel=Gas) transmission trunk carrying South Pars gas; PipelineType=transmission is right. FUEL/FUELSOURCE confirmed: South Pars gas field (offshore-technology, Wikipedia, dialogue.earth all agree). DUPLICATE CHECK against the 8-pipeline roster: NOT a duplicate. It shares the Asaluyeh origin with IGAT 11 (P0441, Asaluyeh->Azerbaijan) and IGAT 9 (P0448, Asaluyeh->West Azerbaijan) but those are domestic Iranian trunks to the NW; P0452 is the export line south/east to Pakistan. Distinct from Iran-Oman (P2225) and the Gazprom/Russia line (P7104). No relabel/segment double-count found.

validity.recommendation: Review LengthKnown down: sum of Iran (~1,100-1,172 km) + Pakistan (~780-785 km) sections is ~1,880-1,960 km, not 2,775 km.
validity.researcher_notes: LENGTH DISAGREEMENT (material). GEM records LengthKnown=2,775 km. offshore-technology.com (a source GEM itself cites for this row) states total length '1,880km'. Wikipedia headlines '2,775 kilometre' but its own body gives Iran section 1,172 km + Pakistan section 785 km = ~1,957 km, so the 2,775 figure is internally inconsistent and appears to be the legacy Iran-Pakistan-INDIA (IPI) full-route length, not the Asaluyeh->Nawabshah line GEM has entered. Independent sources put the actual Iran+Pakistan pipe at ~1,880-1,960 km. Flagging as a spec concern rather than silently passing; recommend correcting to the ~1,880 km figure (offshore-technology) or ~1,957 km (sum of Wikipedia's section lengths). DIAMETER caveat: GEM's single Diameter=56 in is the Iran section spec; the Pakistan section is designed at 42 in per offshore-technology - the row cannot capture both but 56 in is defensible as the built Iranian portion.

validity.recommendation: Clear StartYear1=2024 - the pipeline has never entered operation; no operational start occurred.
validity.researcher_notes: DATE CONCERN. GEM records StartYear1=2024 (with a blank Start [ref]). Nothing supports a 2024 operational start: every independent source through Jan 2026 describes the project as stalled/never commissioned, with the Pakistan section unbuilt (land in Gwadar not even acquired) and Pakistan now moving to shelve it (see status review). StartYear1 is a commissioning-year field, so 2024 is unsupported and contradicted by the evidence; it should be cleared (or, if it was meant as a projected start, removed given the shelving). No verifiable ref exists for a 2024 start, so none is fabricated.

validity.recommendation: Consider adding the Pakistan-side owner (ISGS / PipeCo SPV) - Owner=100% Iran Ministry of Petroleum omits the cross-border ownership split.
validity.researcher_notes: OWNER caveat. GEM records Owner1=Iran Ministry of Petroleum, 100% (blank ref). The Iranian section is owned/operated via the National Iranian Gas Export Company (NIGEC), a subsidiary of the Iran Ministry of Petroleum, so the Iran-portion attribution is reasonable. But the Pakistan section is a Pakistani responsibility - Inter State Gas Systems (ISGS) and, per offshore-technology, a special-purpose vehicle 'PipeCo' with SNGPL/SSGCL/FWO for EPC. A 100%-Iran owner for the whole cross-border line is a simplification, not clearly wrong for the built Iranian portion. Left as a caveat, not filling a ref that would assert 100% Iran ownership of the entire line (unverifiable).

fills.researcher_notes: Both sources state the gas is supplied from Iran's South Pars field. offshore-technology: 'South Pars field which is the world's biggest natural gas field'. Wikipedia: South Pars gas field, Bushehr Province.

Origin: Asaluyeh/Assaluyeh in the Pars energy zone, Bushehr province, Iran (both sources). Terminus: offshore-technology explicitly gives the Pakistan section running 'from Pakistan border to Nawabshah' (Sindh), matching GEM. Caveat: Wikipedia's infobox now states the terminus as Multan, Punjab - the planned end-point has shifted in some accounts; Nawabshah is the historical agreement terminus and is corroborated by offshore-technology. Medium tier due to this endpoint ambiguity.

Both sources give an estimated project cost of US$7.5 billion (offshore-technology: '$7.5bn'; Wikipedia: 'US$7.5 billion'), matching GEM's SegmentCost=7,500,000,000 USD. (Some older 2017 reports cited ~$7bn; the $7.5bn figure is the current corroborated estimate.)

Cannot supply a ref: StartYear1=2024 is unsupported and contradicted by the evidence (pipeline never entered operation; Pakistan section unbuilt). See the spec-concern validity object recommending StartYear1 be cleared. No fabricated ref added (standing rule 2).

Not filling: the recorded 100%-Iran-Ministry-of-Petroleum ownership cannot be corroborated for the whole cross-border line - the Iranian section is via NIGEC (a Ministry subsidiary) but the Pakistan section is owned/built by Pakistani entities (ISGS / PipeCo SPV, SNGPL/SSGCL/FWO). See the attribution validity caveat. Left unresolved pending an owner-split decision.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Recorded Status=construction (LastUpdated 2025-07-11) overstates activity and is now outdated. NEWEST evidence (Jan 2026, multiple independent outlets): Pakistan has formally conveyed to Iran a decision to shelve/abandon the IP pipeline under an out-of-court settlement framework, citing US sanctions, weak domestic gas demand, and IP gas priced above prevailing LNG (Qatar supplying 24 LNG cargoes in 2026), while offering to revive only if the US grants a sanctions waiver. propakistani (2026-01-13), Pipeline Technology Journal ('Pakistan Seeks to Abandon Iran Gas Pipeline Project...'), and Profit/Pakistan Today (2026-01-15) report this independently. Context: the Iranian ~900 km section is built, but the Pakistan section never entered real construction - the Feb 2024 approval of an 80 km border->Gwadar first phase never broke ground (Gwadar land not acquired) and Reuters (Apr 2024) called it 'stalled'. Proposing Status=shelved with ShelvedYear=2026: the project is halted indefinitely by the party responsible for the unbuilt section, but I stop short of 'cancelled' because (a) revival is explicitly offered contingent on a US waiver and (b) Iran is contesting via arbitration and extending the sale agreement - so it is not definitively terminated. ShelvedCancelledType left unset (this is evidence-based, not a dormancy inference, so 'Presumed' does not apply; a human may set 'Confirmed' once the out-of-court settlement is finalized).

summary: Real, correctly-classified IP gas trunk (existence solid, not a duplicate); staged status change construction->shelved (ShelvedYear=2026, high tier, Jan-2026 Pakistan shelving); spec concerns on LengthKnown (2,775 km likely the legacy IPI-to-India figure vs ~1,880 km actual) and StartYear1=2024 (never operated); attribution caveat on 100%-Iran owner; filled FuelSource/Location/SegmentCost refs; Start and Owner refs UNRESOLVED.
